html:
SMTO-SKL-0020 — The calendar times don't make a valid time period

GUID: 36e6d0f2-2dcd-5064-9217-f53132499383
Slug: google-calendar-invalid-time-range
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • The start and end times SMTO was given don't describe one clear period. For example, the end is before the start, the time zone is missing, or the date range is too long. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Give the start and end with the time zone, for example "Tuesday 3 pm to 4 pm, New York time". Make sure the end is after the start. Without a time zone, or with the end first, SMTO can't tell exactly when the event happens.
  2. For an all-day event, say which days it covers. If you're changing an event's time zone or making it all-day, also give the new start and end. SMTO needs the full new times to change how an event is timed.
  3. When searching your calendar, keep the date range to under a year; when checking free or busy times, keep it to about three months. Longer ranges than these are refused.
  4. If the time falls when the clocks change for daylight saving, pick a time that exists that day, or say which of the repeated hours you mean. Some times are skipped or happen twice on those days, so SMTO can't tell which one you mean.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the request and the event or search shows the times you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the times and time zone you asked for, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Calendar time validation rejected the request: malformed or ambiguous timestamps (missing offset or timezone, offset not matching the timezone, DST gap or fold), end not after start, a query window over 366 days (93 for freebusy), or a timezone/all-day change without new start/end.

What this means

  • Time validation rejects malformed/ambiguous timestamps, invalid event ordering or query duration, inconsistent all-day/timezone changes, or invalid provider freebusy intervals. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Time validation rejects malformed/ambiguous timestamps, invalid event ordering or query duration, inconsistent all-day/timezone changes, or invalid provider freebusy intervals.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish user time input from malformed provider interval data and inspect offsets, DST and exclusive all-day end.

How to fix it

  • Supply end after start with an explicit UTC offset or IANA timeZone, keep event searches within 366 days and freebusy within 93 days, and include start/end whenever changing timezone or all_day. For a DST fold give the exact offset, for a DST gap choose an existing local time; all-day end dates are exclusive.
  • Supply end after start, an explicit offset or IANA timezone, and a supported bounded query window. For a DST fold supply its exact offset; choose an existing local time for a gap. All-day end dates are exclusive.

Retry and execution caution

  • Supply end after start, an explicit offset or IANA timezone, and a supported bounded query window. For a DST fold supply its exact offset; choose an existing local time for a gap. All-day end dates are exclusive.

How to verify the fix

  • An unambiguous supported interval is used, and provider busy periods validate before interpretation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
